title: Social workers protest in Pleven for higher wages
seoTitle: Pleven social workers protest for higher wages

tea.why: Social workers are protesting due to low wages, harsh working conditions during field visits, and a lack of proper recognition for their labor.
tea.want: Protesters demand a 350-euro salary increase, funding for clothing and glasses, the restoration of the length-of-service bonus, and fair labor evaluation.
tea.changed: Nov 23, 2026: Social workers in Pleven held a one-hour effective protest as part of ongoing preparations for a nationwide strike.

summary: Employees of the Social Assistance Directorate in Pleven held a one-hour effective protest on November 23, 2026. The action was organised by the Podkrepa Union of Administrative Employees under the motto "Justice and Equal Rights." Protesters gathered to demand a flat 350-euro salary increase, proper evaluation of their heavy fieldwork, allowances for clothing and eyewear, and the reinstatement of the service-length bonus. Union representatives pointed out that low wages and difficult conditions—including facing assaults in the field—have driven high staff turnover and deterred young applicants. The one-hour stoppage served as preparation for a planned national mass strike.
demands: Fair and dignified evaluation of labor
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Social workers in Pleven held a one-hour protest demanding higher wages and better working conditions.
